P.h: BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day exploited since late August
P.p: BeyondTrust Remote Support 26.2.3 and earlier has a critical authentication bypass and arbitrary file upload flaw, scored 9.3. Unauthenticated attackers can perform file operations, escalate to root and reach credential vaults. A suspected Chinese state-sponsored group, Armory Castle (UNC5221), has used it to drop webshells such as BARECLAW.
P.s: Patches for self-hosted customers shipped in October. CISA and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security advise restricting external access to appliances and running forensic reviews for signs of compromise.

items.h: Meta Muse share links expose users' personal and business secrets
items.d: Claroc found 6,800 share links via passive DNS. Conversation titles sat in subdomains, so they were searchable. Samples included revenue reviews, loan applications and bank-fraud details. Meta paused sharing on October 20.

items.h: Hacker used AI agents on Cairn to breach 100+ sites
items.d: Reportedly including John Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins, in about 23 hours. NorForge found 20+ exposed Cairn panels; Trufflehog verified 11% of the secrets it found as valid.

items.h: Romulus ClickFix platform delivers Legion Loader
items.d: Fake landing pages get users to run PowerShell that stages trojanized MSI installers or encrypted archives. Six IP addresses ran the platform. Chrome now adds ClickFix detection to Enhanced Protection.

items.h: AWS Lambda Web Functions are public by default
items.d: No authentication by default, role credentials sit in environment variables, and existing lambda:* grants cover them. SCPs and visibility tooling may miss shadow functions.

P.h: Microsoft says AI agents are like insider threats
P.p: Microsoft added Guardian Agents and agent detection in Defender to protect enterprises from AI agents acting as insider threats. CEO Satya Nadella and security chief Hayete Gallot warned that frontier models cannot be trusted because they are unpredictable and lack organizational norms.
P.s: The advice is to separate the supply of intelligence from authority over it, using independent monitoring. TLDR IT also notes the best automation candidates are reversible, bounded and observable. TLDR InfoSec covers Microsoft's quicksand sandbox repo for AI agents.

tiles.t: AWS brings native PyTorch to Trainium
tiles.d: TorchNeuron enters public beta. Amazon will also contribute upstream to PyTorch to reduce CUDA lock-in.
Cloud Run, GKE and managed Kafka were disrupted, hitting banking, delivery and property services.
Single forward pass, typed outputs with confidence scores. Open weights promised soon.

tiles.t: Zoom adds a Unified Context Layer
tiles.d: New MCP servers and Search & Ask APIs are available now.
2.8 trillion parameters, a move to rely less on OpenAI.

P.h: Anthropic replaces Git for its monorepo with Scion
P.p: Anthropic built Scion, a centralized source control system for tens of millions of daily CI checkouts. It uses content-addressed storage, server-side repository operations and tiered caches. The result is a 200 times smaller source-control CPU and memory footprint than its earlier Git mirroring setup.
P.s: TLDR DevOps also covers The New Stack's view on agents versus Kubernetes: operators for deterministic reconciliation, agents for unclear paths, with autonomy phased from read-only to approved low-risk changes.

tiles.t: tsrs: Cloudflare and VoidZero port TypeScript to Rust
tiles.d: Up to 8x faster and about 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0, and it runs in WebAssembly.
Managed ingress that lets up to 25 services share one load balancer. No extra charge.
Turnkey threat detection for Kubernetes, in preview.
From $2.43 to $0.77 per review via shared prompt-cache prefixes. Cheaper setups missed some findings.
Split fetch and install phases with Landlock and Seatbelt sandboxes (TLDR InfoSec).

items.h: Internet on alert: 8 compromised TLS certificates
items.d: The eight intermediate certificates belong to India-based CA eMudhra Limited and were defective at a level engineers thought impossible.

items.h: PHP warns of two critical RCE flaws, patches due tomorrow
items.d: Believed to affect PHP versions 5 through 8. Emergency patches are expected on October 22.

items.h: DHS bans DeepSeek from federal civilian agencies
items.d: Cites sensitive data possibly stored or processed in China. Agencies get 60 days to request exceptions.

items.h: Anthropic S-1 shows fast growth and huge compute costs
items.d: The draft prospectus reports a net loss above $80 billion in the first half, and says it could spend $750 billion on compute.
